items: Wide QRS, 20 to 40 a minute, no P waves
Never suppress it: no lidocaine or amiodarone

memory_line: Wide and slow is a lifeline, not a target.
caption_lesson:
🌙 Night shift, 3:40 AM. He's 79, heart failure, on telemetry (heart monitor).
• Wide, slow, regular beats at 32 a minute. No P waves
• BP (blood pressure) 82/50, pale, drowsy

❌ 3 mistakes
1️⃣ Called it "slow VT" and never read the rate or the P waves
2️⃣ Gave lidocaine to suppress it, never questioned a rate of 32
3️⃣ No pads, no BP check
➡️ The wide beats stopped. Flat line, no pulse. Code blue.

🔍 Wide QRS? Look at the rate

🟢 Idioventricular rhythm (LIFELINE)
• 20 to 40 beats a minute, wide QRS (the beat's main spike), no P waves
• The ventricles' own backup pacemaker. It shows up when the pacemakers above it fail
• It's keeping him alive. Suppress it and nothing is left

🔴 Ventricular tachycardia (RACE)
• Also wide, but over 100 a minute
• A different rhythm with a different plan

✅ The right move
• Check him: pulse, BP, how he looks
• Pads on now. Atropine or transcutaneous pacing (through the skin), as ordered
• Call now. Never suppress an escape rhythm with lidocaine or amiodarone
• Find the cause: heart block, potassium, drugs that slow the heart

🧠 Wide and slow is a lifeline, not a target.
share_line: 📤 Send this to the nurse who'd try to suppress every wide beat.

Amiodarone injection prescribing information (DailyMed): contraindicated in marked sinus bradycardia and second- or third-degree AV block without a working pacemaker

rn_checks: Idioventricular (ventricular escape) rhythm: 20 to 40 a minute, wide QRS, no related P waves; appears when higher pacemakers fail

Suppressing a ventricular escape rhythm can remove the only pacemaker: lidocaine and amiodarone are contraindicated in severe conduction block or marked bradycardia without a working pacemaker (lidocaine and amiodarone labels)
Accelerated idioventricular rhythm (40 to 100, often after reperfusion) is not taught here, to keep it simple. OK?
